# Hydronephrosis

Canonical hierarchy: All Categories > Basic > Nuclear Medicine > Genitourinary Basic > Hydronephrosis
Canonical deck path: Corebook::Nuclear Medicine::Genitourinary Basic::Hydronephrosis
Primary source posture: RadPrimer supplies the canonical hierarchy/backbone; STATdx supplies supplemental depth and the default source-preferred image replacements when the same image appears in both sources.
Core evidence: no auditable Core Radiology source was supplied in this bundle, so Core-specific support is not asserted.

## Source Coverage And Image Gate

The staged image_evidence files were inspected before duplicate classification. STATdx exactly duplicates 20 of the 22 RadPrimer images as same screenshot/graphic/case-correlation content, usually with a larger 1000 px evidence export versus the 900 px RadPrimer export. Those exact RadPrimer duplicates are archive-optional, while their STATdx counterparts are selected for default teaching/download. STATdx does not cover RadPrimer images 13-14; that same-patient bone-scan/CT correlation cluster remains selected.

## Fused Teaching Backbone

### Definition And Purpose

- [Both] Hydronephrosis is dilation of the renal collecting system, often with renal enlargement, due to impaired urinary outflow; the cause may be mechanical/anatomic or functional.
- [Both] Mechanical causes include ectopic ureter, ureteral stenosis, UPJ stenosis, nephrolithiasis, urothelial or pelvic mass, prostate/bladder outlet pathology, ureterocele, posterior urethral valve, retroperitoneal fibrosis, and extrinsic adenopathy or mass.
- [Both] Functional or nonobstructive dilation can reflect abnormal peristalsis, patulous collecting systems after prior obstruction, urinary diversion, or persistent hydronephrosis after an obstruction has resolved.
- [Both] Tc-99m MAG3 renal scintigraphy characterizes hydronephrosis as obstructed versus dilated but nonobstructed and estimates differential renal function.
- [STATdx] Curves must be correlated with the raw images because duplicated collecting systems, ROI placement over bladder/diaper activity, motion, and anatomy can make curve-only interpretation misleading.

### Protocol And Measurement

- [Both] Patient preparation includes hydration, voiding before the study, and avoidance of furosemide/diuretics on the day of the exam; full bladder, incomplete voiding, bladder outlet obstruction, or reflux can complicate interpretation.
- [STATdx] Catheterization should be considered when voiding is unreliable, such as non-potty-trained children or neurogenic bladder.
- [Both] MAG3 is preferred for hydronephrosis evaluation because tubular extraction preserves image quality even with reduced GFR; DTPA is less robust in low GFR and is usually reserved for GFR calculations.
- [Both] Typical acquisition includes posterior supine flow images, dynamic imaging for 20-30 minutes, furosemide after the collecting system fills, and additional postfurosemide imaging for 20-30 minutes.
- [Both] Adults commonly receive 40 mg IV furosemide with normal creatinine; azotemia may require higher doses, and pediatric dosing is weight based.
- [Both] Differential renal function is normally about 45-55% per kidney. Reported values should be trended over time because loss of relative function can be more important than a single borderline value.
- [STATdx] Each exam offers three opportunities to clear a kidney or moiety: prefurosemide washout, postfurosemide washout, and gravity-assisted drainage/postvoid imaging. Once a kidney or moiety clears, later t1/2 values add little.

### Renogram Pattern Categories

- [Both] Normal: prompt uptake, cortical peak around 2-3 minutes, calyceal activity by about 5 minutes, bladder activity by 10-15 minutes, spontaneous washout before furosemide, and t1/2 <= 10 minutes.
- [Both] Dilated but unobstructed: collecting-system activity may rise until furosemide or GAD, then washes out normally; differential renal function is usually normal unless prior obstruction caused damage.
- [STATdx] GAD supports nonobstruction when clearance is > 50% and supports obstruction when clearance is < 50%; adding GAD improves specificity for furosemide renography.
- [Both] Partial obstruction: excretion is delayed and may improve but not normalize after furosemide or GAD; t1/2 is indeterminate at 10-20 minutes and obstructed when > 20 minutes, with higher t1/2 suggesting higher-grade obstruction.
- [Both] High-grade or complete obstruction: delayed/asymmetric flow, delayed or absent collecting-system visualization, low differential function, progressive collecting-system activity despite furosemide/GAD, and very high or unmeasurable t1/2.
- [Both] Severely dilated but nonobstructed systems may need a more permissive t1/2 cutoff around 15 minutes depending on the clinical scenario.

### Mimics, Pitfalls, And Differential

- [Both] Vesicoureteral reflux can mimic obstruction, especially if the bladder is not catheterized; reflux and obstruction can coexist.
- [Both] Acute tubular necrosis may show delayed nephrogram and minimal excretion, especially in transplant kidneys, but is not a collecting-system obstruction.
- [Both] Renal artery stenosis can cause asymmetric reduced flow, delayed nephrogram, smaller kidney, and low relative function while washout may remain normal.
- [STATdx] Renal vein thrombosis can mimic high-grade obstruction with reduced flow, delayed nephrogram, and poor collecting-system visualization.
- [STATdx] Low GFR, dehydration, poor response to furosemide, full bladder, immature kidneys, and atonic/severely dilated systems can create false-positive or indeterminate scans; many improve with GAD.
- [Both] CT, MR urography, ultrasound, and bone scan/PET examples provide anatomic or incidental correlation; anatomic dilation can persist after relief of obstruction, so functional assessment may still be needed.

### Clinical Course And Management

- [Both] High-grade obstruction requires treatment to avoid renal functional impairment. Mechanical relief options include stent, nephrostomy, pyeloplasty, urinary diversion, and lithotripsy depending on cause.
- [Both] Low-grade or partial obstruction is often followed with serial renograms to evaluate resolution and monitor for decreasing differential renal function.
- [STATdx] If GAD clearance is > 50% and function is stable, conservative management is supported; if clearance remains < 50% or differential renal function declines, obstruction is more likely clinically significant.

## Selected Image Atlas For Future Generation

Use the following primary images by default. Archive-optional RadPrimer images are retained for audit/completeness only because they are exact duplicate exports of selected STATdx images.

- STATdx image 1: interpretive curve graphic for normal, dilated-unobstructed, partial obstruction, and high-grade obstruction patterns.
- STATdx image 2: normal symmetric MAG3 uptake and excretion.
- STATdx images 3-5: MAG3 pattern set for high-grade obstruction, bilateral partial obstruction, and dilated but unobstructed/patulous system.
- STATdx image 6: vesicoureteral reflux/nonfunctioning right kidney example, with motion artifact also noted as a possible mimic.
- STATdx image 7: renal artery stenosis mimic with small delayed right kidney and reduced relative function.
- STATdx images 8-9: atomic bone-scan/CECT stone-obstruction cluster in the same patient.
- STATdx images 10-11: atomic persistent-dilation/indeterminate-washout cluster in the same patient, favoring low GFR or dehydration rather than active obstruction.
- STATdx images 12-13: renal artery stenosis retention and ectopic ureter/clamped nephrostomy high-grade obstruction examples.
- STATdx images 14-15: atomic urinary-diversion/patulous nonobstructed collecting-system cluster with CT correlation.
- STATdx images 16-19: complete obstruction/renal vein thrombosis mimic, transplant ATN, reflux hydronephrosis, and malignant extrinsic obstruction examples.
- STATdx images 20-23: selected exact replacements for RadPrimer UPJ obstruction graphic, composite anomaly renogram, 6-week-old left UPJ obstruction renogram, and right UPJ obstruction renogram.
- STATdx image 24: sparse-caption Gallbladder Activity source image retained for source completeness and possible pitfall review; downweight for routine generators unless specifically relevant.
- RadPrimer images 13-14: unique same-patient bone-scan/CT correlation showing a duplicated left collecting system with dilated upper pole moiety and parapelvic cyst explanation; keep as an atomic cluster.

## Downstream Use Notes

- Use selectedPrimaryImageIds for default image download and teaching.
- Treat archiveOptionalImageIds as audit/completeness records, not as default card or lecture images.
- Preserve atomic case clusters listed in the manifest when generating future narrative or cards.
- Keep human-facing prose labels clean, such as STATdx image 4 or RadPrimer image 14. Use short IDs such as SDX-04 and RP-14 only in registry, filenames, and traceability fields.

imageRegistry.caption: Graphic shows potential activity curves in a Tc-99m MAG3 exam done for the evaluation of hydronephrosis. The red curve represents normal biexponential excretion. Green represents a dilated, but unobstructed, system that clears after the administration of furosemide. Blue represents a system that is partially obstructed as demonstrated by partial response to furosemide. Yellow represents high-grade obstruction. In reality, not all cases fall neatly into 1 of these categories and should be assessed for anatomic variants, such as duplicated systems. Always correlate graph with raw images to corroborate findings and exclude technical error.

expanded protocol details for catheterization scenarios, pediatric MAG3 dosing, DTPA limitations with low GFR, and full-bladder/dehydration pitfalls
pitfall examples including duplicated collecting-system ROI errors, urinary bladder/diaper contamination, motion artifact, renal vein thrombosis mimic, low GFR/dehydration, and immature kidneys

sourceSelectionPlan.imageCurationPolicy: Exact duplicates may be archived; near duplicates and conceptual replacements remain selected as recognition reinforcement unless visually identical or unusable. Download only selectedPrimaryImageIds by default.
sourceSelectionPlan.duplicateEvidencePolicy: ExactDuplicate decisions require visual evidence from image_evidence files, same stable source image ID, image hashes, or explicit manual/source confirmation. Caption-only or topic-only similarity is marked uncertain/nearDuplicate and kept primary.

caseClusterGuardrails.rule: Same-patient, follow-up, procedure, adjacent-slice, comparison-view, and time-lapse clusters are atomic teaching clusters.
caseClusterGuardrails.note: No source case cluster was intentionally split. RadPrimer images 13-14 remain together because STATdx does not cover that duplicated left collecting-system/parapelvic cyst correlation cluster; STATdx images 10-11 remain together as a separate same-patient persistent-dilation/indeterminate-washout cluster.
